ARCS kitOrganism 53cold-read

Cold Read

Give a reader with zero context the whole page in one glance: who, what, where, when and why as labelled slots, how as before, during and after with real timing, and one line on how to read the rest.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Slot labelKit 27 section label (mono caps, label size), one per slot, in a fixed column on wide screensmuted
2Slot answerBody size, full ink; hairline between slotstext, border
3How stepsThree cells in order, before, during, after: label, timing line (small, semibold), one sentence; a short connector between cellssurface, border, label muted (colour never decorates)
4How to readKit 31 callout, one lineKit 31 callout in a neutral variant: surface-2 and border; gold stays for limits and gaps

Usage

Use it when

  • A page a reader may open cold: a proposal, a brief, a leave-behind (rule 13a).
  • The timing has real dates or a real trigger to state.

Do not use it when

  • An internal page whose readers already have the context.
  • There is no real why-now; say so in the When slot instead of inventing urgency.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
slots[][label, text] pairsyesIn the order of rule 13a: Why, What, then Who and Where if needed, then When, which states the real trigger (why now) or says there is none.
how[][label, when, text] triplesnoBefore, during, after, each with a real date or time, or "not booked yet"; never a vague relative.
readstringnoOne line on how to read the page.

Access

  • Slots are a <dl>: each label is a <dt>, each answer its <dd>, read in order.
  • The steps are an ordered list with an accessible name, so the sequence survives without the visual connector.
  • Static and always open: a cold-read header is never folded, so nothing it says is hidden; nothing is interactive; prints whole.
